content: Chloral hydrate is a sedative medication prescribed for short-term use to treat insomnia, helping patients fall asleep and maintain sleep for adequate rest. It is also used to alleviate anxiety and induce sleep before surgical procedures. Additionally, it may be prescribed post-surgery to manage pain and to treat symptoms of alcohol withdrawal. If you have questions about other potential uses, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Chloral hydrate is available in several forms: capsules, liquid for oral use, and rectal suppositories. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you need clarification. Take the medication exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. For the liquid form, mix it with half a glass of water, fruit juice, or ginger ale, and drink it immediately. Swallow capsules whole with a full glass of water or fruit juice; do not chew them. If using a suppository, follow these steps: 1. Remove the wrapper. 2. Moisten the tip of the suppository with water. 3. Lie on your left side and bring your right knee to your chest (left-handed individuals should lie on their right side and raise their left knee). 4. Insert the suppository into the rectum, approximately ½ to 1 inch for infants and children, and 1 inch for adults. Hold it in place briefly. 5. Stand up after about 15 minutes. 6. Wash your hands thoroughly and resume your normal activities. Chloral hydrate has the potential to be habit-forming. Do not take larger doses, use it more frequently, or continue treatment longer than directed by your doctor. Even if you feel well, continue taking the medication as prescribed. If you have been using chloral hydrate in large doses or for an extended period, do not stop abruptly; consult your doctor, who will likely taper your dose gradually. Before starting chloral hydrate, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to it, aspirin, tartrazine (a yellow dye found in some foods and medications), or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), antihistamines, furosemide, medications for depression or seizures, sedatives, sleeping pills, tranquilizers, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of kidney or liver disease, heart or stomach problems, asthma, or substance abuse. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking chloral hydrate, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking this medication. Be aware that chloral hydrate may cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can enhance the sedative effects of this medication, so avoid consuming it. To minimize stomach upset, take chloral hydrate with food or milk. If you miss a dose, skip it entirely and take the next dose at the scheduled time. Do not double doses to make up for a missed one. Chloral hydrate may cause side effects. Minor side effects include drowsiness, upset stomach, vomiting, and diarrhea. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, such as skin rash, itching, confusion, difficulty breathing, slow heartbeat, or extreme fatigue, require immediate medical attention. If you experience a severe reaction, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store chloral hydrate in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and protect the liquid form from light. Do not freeze the liquid. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly; consult your pharmacist for guidance. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Keep all medical appointments while using chloral hydrate. If you have diabetes, use TesTape or Clinistix to monitor your urine for sugar, as chloral hydrate can interfere with Clinitest results. Do not share this medication with others, as it is a controlled substance. Prescription refills are limited; consult your pharmacist if you have questions. Chloral hydrate is sold under the brand names Aquachloral®, Aquachloral Supprettes®, and Noctec®.
